Hi Ethan — thanks again for the time. I pulled answers together from product and infra; below is a concise response you can share with your security team. I also attached our SOC 2 evidence stub for context (SOC2_evidence_stub.pdf).

1) Region pinning guarantees
- For pinned tenants we provide 2 modes: logical pinning and strict physical pinning. Logical pinning ensures requests are routed to nearest compatible region by default, with tenant metadata ensuring primary routing preference. Strict physical pinning provisions dedicated capacity in the target region so inference, logs, and ephemeral caches are resident and never leave the region except under customer-approved DR actions.
- We recommend strict physical pinning for regulated workloads. This is available as an add-on and includes an SLA addendum.

2) Cross-region failover and PII controls
- Cross-region failover is opt-in for pinned tenants. If enabled, we keep a minimal, encrypted failover path that contains only non-PII operational metadata needed to route traffic. Actual request payloads and request logs remain in-region unless the customer enables cross-region replication for DR.
- If a customer wants zero replication, we can disable automated failover and instead support manual runbook-driven failover (you get a documented procedure and a one-click authorization from your SecOps).

3) Backups and snapshots
- Backups of KV caches and model state are configurable. Defaults: 7-day retention, stored encrypted at rest in the pinned region when strict pinning is selected.
- We support custom retention policies and in-region backup storage for up to 7 years if required by policy; automated deletion on request is supported via an authenticated API or through a ticket with our security ops team.

4) Logging and retention
- Request logs are disabled by default for sensitive routes on Dedicated/Private deployments when requested. For hosted customers, we provide route-level control to redact or disable request logging. Logs are stored encrypted and, when strict pinning is selected, remain in-region.

5) Encryption and key management
- All data at rest and in transit is encrypted. For strict pinning we recommend customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) so you control key location and rotation.

Suggested next steps:
- Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra and SecOps. We will include an infra engineer to walk failover runbooks and a product manager to review pinning options and SLA addendum.
- Share any compliance doc checklist items you want addressed ahead of the call and we will pre-populate answers.

Hope this helps — happy to refine.

Best,

Ethan — quick clarifying note from infra: if you choose strict physical pinning + zero replication, DR becomes manual and mean time to recover can be longer. For most customers we run a warm-standby in-region with encrypted snapshots replicated to a secondary in the same legal boundary (eg EU secondary AZ) to balance RTO vs data residency.

If AcmeBank requires both 1) zero replication outside EU and 2) sub-30 min automated failover, we will need a dedicated cross-region architecture inside the EU (separate availability zone pairs) and an SLA amendment. We can put cost estimates in the proposal.

Also proposing two times for the technical deep-dive: Tue 2027-03-16 10:00-11:00 ET or Wed 2027-03-17 09:00-10:00 ET. Which works better for your infra team?

Thanks,
